Over Two Hundred Attend NORML Conference In Washington D.C. --
Opening On C-Span; Full Conference On The Internet

The 1998 NORML conference, November 12-14th, seemed to be a success in every way. While an attendance of roughly 250 attendees and speakers, et al., represents only one millionth of the DEAland population, it was a good turn-out for an organization with such limited resources. It is remarkable that the tiny and already over-worked NORML staff was able to organize such an event.

The fact that C-Span carried the opening morning session, with speeches by NORML founder Keith Stroup, NORML Board Chairman Dan Viets, and a representative of the George Soros funded Lindesmith Center, gave NORML valuable national exposure. (C-Span reruns the tape of these events for several days.)

Carrying the conference live on the Internet was important as recognition of the role of the Internet in the movement. This effort was a collaboration between High Times Magazine and www.myhouse.com – NORML’s Internet service provider. In the future this will be a much more important aspect of the event.

Obviously, coming in the wake of the successful medical marijuana initiatives and other favorable events, the tone was one of optimism. Also, the absence of any "competition" from a Drug Policy Foundation conference made the event stand out. (The DPF has lost its funding from Soros and is struggling, so its future is uncertain.)

First, it has to be said that the real measure of the success of any conference depends on what happens after everyone goes home. I have been to many conferences that felt great, but were really a waste of everyone’s time. The fact that NORML is able to build on this conference is what is really important.

The most enjoyable event at the conference was a lunch-break presentation on the history of marijuana-music by Dr. John P. Morgan, --yes, the co-author of Marijuana Myths; Marijuana Facts. At the opposite extreme, it is always agonizing to hear the stories of the victims of the war on marijuana.

One of the most interesting presentations was given by Dr. Geoffrey Guy, who is growing the first legal medical marijuana crops in the UK.
See

I talked about the meaning of legalizing marijuana in a social and political context. What it really means is the repudiation of a century of lying. This is not just about changing laws. If that was all that is involved, it would be relatively simple. I think that even most people on our side do not fully understand the impact that repudiating the lies will have.

As usual, the most notable negative at the conference was the almost all-white nature of the attendance. When I was National Director I used to joke that NORML was the whitest organization that I belonged to – that didn’t have a golf course.

The truth is that there is no group that would be more welcoming to people of color. And there is a terrible irony that the marijuana laws were generally racist in their origin – as was illustrated by Dr. Morgan’s presentation on marijuana music. The even greater irony is that most "minority leaders" are prohibitionists, who presumably will not be satisfied until the white establishment has locked up all of the non-whites  -- for their own good, of course. Unfortunately, NORML does not have the resources to recruit adequately in the non-white communities – or in the white community either. Perhaps the Internet can help in that regard.

The Internet is even more likely to bring more young people in. I really enjoyed meeting the college students who told me that they read Marijuananews!

When I go to a NORML conference, the pleasure of seeing old friends – and meeting new ones --can get in the way of critical assessments of how well things are really going. However, I think that this conference will be remembered as the beginning of a new era in the marijuana reform movement. But as I said, the important thing is what happens now that the conference is over.
